title: A posting date in a closed period lands in QB Unexported
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure QuickBooks Online's closing date is the last day of last month.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one approved line with one stock part picked from inventory at a cost of $40.00 each, quantity 2.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Set the posting date to a day of last month.
  4. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  5. Open QB Unexported in ShopView.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The date shows.

Step 4:

  • The work order is Closed: Close succeeds.

Step 5:

  • The entry is under Journal Entries with QuickBooks's closed-period error, work order 1's number, its classification and the type "Internal Work Order Close", with Export and Mark as Exported.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-N3: “If the posting date falls in a closed period, QuickBooks rejects the entry and it lands in QB Unexported under Journal Entries with the QuickBooks error text, the work order number and the classification (type "Internal Work Order Close", "Internal Work Order Reopen" or "No Charge line"), with Export and Mark as Exported as for other rows.”
  • S3-E3: “If the posting date is in a closed accounting period, Close succeeds; QuickBooks returns its closed-period error and the entry lands in QB Unexported as any other rejected entry does today; AccountingHub holds it (Story 8).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
